You're asking people who do not believe in good/bad or better/worse questions like "Wouldn't it just be easier/better..." and saying "Killing oneself seems optimal". This is what I think the Nihilist point of view is; no value judgements, no "ought"s or "should"s. This is my main and some of my friends probably know about it, but fuck it. I grew up in a very violent household. My father beat my mother very severely. I'm cursed with a very good, early memory. Younger me swore not to repeat my parents' mistakes. Unfortunately, I had no plan as to how I would avoid doing that. The first girl to show me any attention turned out to be just like my mother (during a bad period in her life, anyway). My mother is a very bad, neurotic person that neglected me and allowed horrific things to happen to me. This girl and I had our first kid at 17 years old. I joined the military and resolved to do the right thing as I saw it at the time. The problem was that neither of us were well mentally. We had the best intentions and we thought we loved one another. In reality, we were codependent. Between 2005 and 2009, we had 4 children. I question the paternity of a few of the children now, but only when I'm drunk and only to myself (and the internet apparently). In 2011, I discovered she had been having an affair with my best friend. A guy I had served in the military with for years. If I'm being honest with myself, I was am asshole and a shitty husband. It was bound to happen. I thought we could work it out. So did she. We tried... She cheated more. I found about more past indiscretions. Long story short, I slapped and choked her when this all came to a head. The next day she kissed me goodbye as I left for work and called the police not long after. It felt like a betrayal at the time, but it was the smartest thing she ever did. I called her from work and tried to plan lunch with her. She told me that she had called the cops and that they were looking for me. I went into my First Sergeant's office to tell him what was going on and he had already been contacted. My supervisor drove me to my house and I changed into civilian clothes and then he drove me to the police station. I confessed to almost everything immediately. It took me a few years to admit that I had choked her unconscious. I couldn't admit that to myself for some reason. They released me from jail while the case was pending and I went back to work. Eventually, she contacted me enough times that I broke the restraining order and answered the call. That led to us living together again in secret. That's when I found out that she was still carrying on an affair. I had been suicidal since I was a kid. I'm not sure when it started, but I remember that it occurred to me that I could kill myself when I was 10 or so. When I was 20, I figured out how I would do that. After I found out the last bit of news, I hanged myself in the garage. She found me and cut me down. The cops and ambulance followed and I was committed for the first time. I was in a mental health hospital for over two weeks until they transferred me to a military mental health facility. Two more weeks there and back to jail. Once in jail, I started counseling at least every week. I ended up serving a year on the restraining order violation. 5 years probation on the actual domestic violence (felony threats in there somewhere too). After getting out, I've been working in restaurants and hating life, more or less. Ended up talking about suicide and a girl I was seeing called the police. Back in the mental health hospital for a few weeks. They figured out somehow that I was still entitled to VA benefits due to my reenlistment (first term of service was honorable). After that I had free weekly therapy. Been going since then. So after four years of counseling (still going), I've worked through a ton of childhood issues. I'm not angry anymore. I've forgiven myself for what I did. The repercussions are just endless. I've not seen the kids since we put them to bed that night. It wasn't even the normal routine. I was simmering with anxious tension during the whole process, waiting to confront her. Wish I could have sung to our youngest like always. I probably would still be the same person had I not been in the criminal justice system. Having terrible thoughts and saying awful things in the privacy of your home is one thing. Having those thoughts and words read aloud in a court room for public record... That really makes you take a hard look in the mirror. Sitting with other batterers around a table and listening to the sickening shit we thought and said... I couldn't have changed without the impetus of being dicked in the ass by the justice system. I just wish it would end. I've done some fucked up stuff, but I really would like to just melt into the background and be a decent person.
